articles.title: Atlantic Highly Migratory Species; Atlantic Highly Migratory Species Southeast Data, Assessment, and Review Workshops Advisory Panel
articles.summary: NMFS solicits nominations for the Atlantic Highly Migratory Species (HMS) SouthEast Data, Assessment, and Review (SEDAR) Workshops Advisory Panel, also known as the "SEDAR Pool." The SEDAR Pool is comprised of a group of individuals who, if selected, review data and advise NMFS on the scientific information, data, and models used in stock assessments for oceanic sharks in the Atlantic Ocean, including the Gulf of America and Caribbean Sea. NMFS is seeking nominations for a 5-year term beginning in 2027. NMFS will consider individuals with definable interests in recreational and commercial fishing and related industries, including those from the environmental community, academia, and non-governmental organizations, for membership on the SEDAR Pool.

articles.title: Compliance Procedure (52 U.S.C. 30109, 30107(a))
Medicare and Medicaid Programs; Organ Procurement Organizations Conditions for Coverage: Revisions to the Conditions for Coverage
articles.summary: This final rule revises the Conditions for Coverage for Organ Procurement Organizations (OPOs) to clarify outstanding procedural questions and provide additional operational flexibility for OPOs to achieve high performance resulting in the successful procurement, distribution, and transplantation of more life-saving organs. This rule revises definitions, revises the designation requirements for OPOs, clarifies when an OPO's service area is open for competition, and updates the process for appeals. We are committed to holding all OPOs accountable for their performance and this final rule does not revise the focus on improving the volume of donors and transplants assessed in the outcome measures or the tier structure used for re-certification and de-certification of OPOs.

articles.summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is taking final action to approve a revision to the Maricopa County Air Quality Department (MCAQD or "Department") portion of the Arizona State Implementation Plan (SIP). This revision establishes a federally enforceable program allowing for the generation of emission reduction credits (ERCs) by retrofitting or replacing existing on-road vehicles with lower emitting vehicles while meeting other Clean Air Act (CAA or "Act") requirements. These ERCs are intended to be used as offsets for major stationary sources under the Department's Nonattainment New Source Review (NNSR) program. The EPA is approving this SIP revision because we find that it meets the applicable CAA requirements.

articles.summary: The transpacific has become the most lucrative major container shipping trade in the world, with carriers generating five times more spot revenue per nautical mile on the Shanghai–Los Angeles route than on shipments to North Europe via the Cape of Good Hope. New analysis from Alphaliner shows that the extraordinary strength of the US trade …
articles.content: Transpacific emerges as liner shipping's golden trade - Splash247 Port of Long Beach The transpacific has become the most lucrative major container shipping trade in the world, with carriers generating five times more spot revenue per nautical mile on the Shanghai–Los Angeles route than on shipments to North Europe via the Cape of Good Hope. New analysis from Alphaliner shows that the extraordinary strength of the US trade has persisted well beyond the traditional peak season, with freight rates approaching levels last seen during the pandemic. At approximately $7,500 per feu, the 5,775 nautical mile Shanghai–Los Angeles voyage generates $1.30 in revenue per container per nautical mile, compared with just 26 cents on Shanghai–Rotterdam via the Cape, or 34 cents via Suez. Shanghai–New York generates 96 cents per nautical mile, with spot rates remaining above $10,000 per feu since late August. These figures represent revenue rather than profit, but nevertheless illustrate the extraordinary divergence between the industry’s principal east–west trades. Carriers are responding by throwing more tonnage at the Pacific. MSC recently upgraded its Sentosa service with 23,600 teu megamaxes, replacing vessels of approximately 15,000 teu. ZIM, which already deploys 52% of its capacity on the Pacific, will launch another China–California service in December. The boom is feeding directly into corporate earnings. COSCO reported third-quarter liner profits of $2.66bn, double the year-earlier

articles.content: Stronger revenue at Uber Freight, but profits still elusive - FreightWaves Uber Freight CEO Rebecca Tinucci took to LinkedIn to tout the company’s third quarter financial performance, which still is a long way from operating profitability. As Tinucci said in her published remarks, “two things can be true at the same time.” Her comments highlighted gross bookings of $1.768 billion, which is a record for the group. It also was a 34% improvement over the third quarter of 2026. Sequentially, Uber Freight (NYSE: UBER) revenue also was up from the second quarter figure of $1.583 billion, an 11.6% gain. But those higher revenues also came with another operating loss, $33 million. That wasn’t what Tinucci focused on in her LinkedIn remarks. Instead, she cited other statistics that were not in the Uber parent company’s prepared statement regarding its earnings. Tinucci said the approximately 35% year-over-year in revenue was “supported by an exceptional 36% volume increase in our U.S. & Canada brokerage.” She added that occurred even though the market featured “relatively flat freight volumes across the industry.” Revenue per load was up about 8% year-over-year, Tinucci said. Loads per day per head, considered in the brokerage business to be one of the key measures of productivity, was up about 10% from the third quarter of 2025. articles.content: Benelux returns to China for LPG carrier brace - Splash247 Huangpu Wenchong Shipbuilding Greek gas shipowner Benelux Overseas has been linked to another pair of midsize gas carriers at China’s Huangpu Wenchong Shipbuilding, adding to its growing orderbook at the CSSC-affiliated yard. Shipbuilding sources have identified the Athens-based company, controlled by Kostas Angelou, as the buyer behind the latest 48,000 cu m two-ship deal, extending a relationship dating back to late 2023. Huangpu Wenchong has confirmed the contract through China Shipbuilding Trading, identifying the customer only as a European shipowner. Pricing and delivery dates have not been disclosed. The conventionally fuelled vessels will be based on the yard’s established 48,000 cu m design, developed by Shanghai Merchant Ship Design and Research Institute (SDARI). The ships will feature three independent fully refrigerated Type A cargo tanks, allowing them to carry LPG and ammonia, among other cargoes. Benelux first turned to Huangpu Wenchong in December 2023, ordering two vessels of the same size with an option for a third, which was exercised in March 2024. The initial pair was reported to cost around $64m apiece. The first vessel from that programme, Olympios Gas (pictured), was completed in July this year. The latest deal adds to the Greek owner’s wider gas carrier expansion, which has also included a move into larger ammonia-capable tonnage. articles.content: Orkim books $38m product tanker pair in China - Splash247 Orkim Malaysian tanker owner Orkim has signed contracts for two more product tankers in China, committing about $37.6m as it presses ahead with fleet expansion following last year’s stock market listing. The Bursa Malaysia-listed company said its wholly owned subsidiary Orkim Marine entered into shipbuilding deals with Fujian Southeast Shipbuilding and Fujian Mawei Shipbuilding. The two 9,000 dwt clean petroleum product tankers are scheduled for completion by the end of 2028 and 2029, respectively, according to the stock exchange filing. The combined investment is equivalent to MYR153.6m. Orkim said it plans to finance the contracts through a combination of internal funds and borrowings, with the final financing structure depending on the timing and size of loan drawdowns. The latest contracts form part of a wider programme to add five more tankers between 2027 and 2029, including the previously contracted Orkim Ruby, a 14,500 dwt product carrier scheduled for next year. Orkim currently operates 21 vessels with a combined carrying capacity of 281,534 dwt, serving Malaysian and regional energy customers. The owner has been expanding its chemical and product tanker exposure since listing on Bursa Malaysia in December 2025. Earlier this year, it acquired the 13,850 dwt Rich Sunda for $24.2m and subsequently agreed to buy the 13,988 dwt Rong Yao Wu Zhou for CNY157m ($23.6m at today’s exchange rate). articles.content: First look: GXO Logistics Q3 revenue hits $3.6B - FreightWaves GXO Logistics reported third-quarter revenue of $3.59 billion, a 5.7% increase from a year earlier, as the global contract logistics provider secured more new business and expanded its sales pipeline to record levels. The Greenwich, Connecticut-based company (NYSE: GXO) said Tuesday that organic revenue grew 6.4% during the quarter ended Sept. 30, its fastest pace in more than three years. GXO also reported $375 million in new business wins, a 34% year-over-year increase and the second consecutive quarter in which new contract wins grew more than 30%. The company’s sales pipeline reached a record $3.1 billion, up more than 30% from a year earlier, signaling continued demand for outsourced warehousing, distribution and supply chain services. “The new strategy we put in motion over the past year is delivering results,” GXO CEO Patrick Kelleher said in a news release. Kelleher said the company is winning more business across its core markets and strategic growth sectors while improving its ability to convert opportunities into revenue. GXO Q3 financial performance GXO reported net income of $65 million, compared with $60 million during the same period in 2025. Diluted earnings per share increased to 56 cents from 51 cents. articles.content: Norway Detains Sanctioned Chinese Vessel Over False Flag Registration Ya Qing Hai Yang off Vesterålen Islands. (Courtesy of Arctic North Adventures) Norway Detains Sanctioned Chinese Vessel Over False Flag Registration Malte Humpert Total Views: 216 November 3, 2026 Norway has detained a Chinese-owned heavy-lift vessel sanctioned for its role in delivering equipment to Russia’s Arctic LNG 2 project, in what appears to be the first known detention in the Arctic of a Chinese vessel linked to Russia’s shadow fleet. The Ya Qing Hai Yang was detained after Norwegian inspectors found that it lacked valid flag-state registration and required certificates, the Norwegian Maritime Authority said. The case is a notable enforcement action against a vessel with documented ties to Russia’s sanctioned energy sector, although authorities say the detention was based on maritime safety and registration deficiencies rather than the ship’s sanctions status. The Norwegian Maritime Authority inspected the vessel on October 13 after it sought shelter from bad weather in Andfjorden, off the Vesterålen Islands in northern Norway. “During the inspection, it was discovered that the vessel did not have a valid flag registration and lacked the required certificates,” Dag Inge Aarhus, the authority’s communications director said last week. “The vessel has therefore been detained until further notice.” The vessel remains off the Vesterålen Islands as of November 3. articles.content: October deluge brings Panama Canal lake levels back towards normal - Splash247 Monjasa A surprisingly wet October has brought much-needed relief to the Panama Canal, with Gatun Lake recovering to near its historical average despite warnings that a powerful El Niño could trigger another prolonged drought. New research from Ursa Shipbrokers, drawing on Panama Canal Authority data, shows Gatun Lake averaged 85.80 ft (26.15 m) over the first 30 days of October, just 0.15 ft below its historical October average. The recovery is particularly striking compared with 2023, when severe drought crippled canal operations. October’s average was 6.04 ft higher than the corresponding month three years ago. The turnaround follows an unusually prolonged decline in lake levels, which continued until August this year rather than bottoming out in May, as is normally the case. Rainfall statistics underline the improvement. Data compiled from the canal authority’s meteorological stations show 303.3 mm of rain fell across the watershed between October 1 and 29, 8.4% above the 30-year average and 83.6% more than during the same period in drought-stricken 2023. By October 29, Gatun Lake’s daily level had reached 86.56 ft, up from an August low of 83.80 ft. Improved conditions have allowed the canal authority to reverse some restrictions. articles.content: Grimaldi lines up 10 car carrier newbuilds in China - Splash247 Grimaldi Italian shipping group Grimaldi is lining up another 10 car carriers at Chinese shipyards, including a series of 11,000 ceu vessels that would become the largest in its fleet. The Naples-based owner has signed letters of intent with China Merchants for five next-generation 10,000 ceu pure car and truck carriers (PCTCs) and with CSSC’s Guangzhou Shipyard International (GSI) for another five ships of 11,000 ceu each. Both designs will have additional capacity for containers and other rolling cargo, extending their capabilities beyond conventional vehicle transportation. The Emanuele Grimaldi-led owner confirmed the agreements, saying the projects would now move from preliminary design to engineering, a process expected to take around six months. Deliveries are targeted for 2030 and 2031. The agreements have yet to translate into firm shipbuilding contracts, with no pricing disclosed for the proposed vessels. The latest move builds on Grimaldi’s extensive car carrier expansion in China. In 2022 and 2023, the group amassed an orderbook of 17 ammonia-ready PCTCs (pictured), comprising 10 ships at China Merchants and seven at CSSC-affiliated yards. The owner has since been taking larger ships into its fleet, most recently the 9,800 ceu Grande Pacifico and Grande Egitto, built by China Merchants Heavy Industries Jiangsu. articles.content: Aker Solutions bags engineering deal for Qatar oilfield redevelopment - Splash247 Aker Solutions Norwegian offshore engineering group Aker Solutions has received a letter of award from Vietnam’s PTSC Mechanical & Construction for work on QatarEnergy’s Maydan Mahzam oilfield redevelopment project. The contract covers detailed engineering for three major topsides, four jackets and modifications required to connect new facilities with existing offshore infrastructure. Aker Solutions describes the award as sizeable, valuing it between NOK500m and NOK1.5bn ($54m to $162m). The company will carry out engineering work from its offices in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, and Mumbai, India. The award remains subject to a final contract, with Aker Solutions expecting to register the order in its Renewables and Field Development segment during the fourth quarter of 2026. The Maydan Mahzam field lies around 100 km northeast of Qatar’s coastline, in water depths of approximately 40 metres. Discovered in the 1960s, the field began producing in 1965. QatarEnergy is undertaking a major redevelopment to modernise ageing offshore facilities, improve production efficiency and extend the field’s operating life. PTSC M&C secured the project’s first major offshore construction package in September and signed the main contract with QatarEnergy on October 22. articles.summary:
Mexican authorities recently destroyed over 52 tons of avocados after discovering the presence of destructive agricultural pests in shipments due for international export.
The post Mexico destroys 52 tons of avocados after pest discovery raises export concerns appeared first on FreightWaves.
articles.content: Mexico destroys 52 tons of avocados after pest discovery raises export concerns - FreightWaves Mexican avocado producers have destroyed up to 52 tons of fruit after authorities detected a destructive agricultural pest in shipments intended for international export to the U.S. and other destinations. The seed weevil pest raises concerns about potential disruptions to U.S.-Mexico avocado trade, which generates an estimated $641.5 million in cross-border transportation and warehousing activity. Environmental officials in Michoacán, Mexico’s largest avocado-producing state, confirmed Sunday that avocado seed weevil larvae had been discovered in fruit destined for export, according to Reuters. The discovery prompted authorities to detain shipments, while growers from Michoacán, Jalisco, Colima and Nayarit destroyed up to 52 tons of avocados over the weekend. Mexico’s National Service of Health, Food Safety and Food Quality (SENASICA) supported the disposal of the fruit as part of efforts to prevent the pest from spreading. Videos circulating on social media showed growers unloading truckloads of avocados into pits, where the fruit was burned and buried under pest-control protocols. The avocado seed weevil can damage fruit by boring into its seed and can spread through orchards, threatening production if infestations are not contained. articles.content: Flexport forwarding volumes up 40% as headcount grows only 5% - FreightWaves Flexport’s freight volumes are up 40% from a year ago while its headcount has grown 5%, founder and CEO Ryan Petersen told FreightWaves. He credits the gap to artificial intelligence tools the company now runs across customs, routing and its own engineering teams. The AI has a limit in customs, the most regulated part of Flexport’s business. There, an AI-generated tariff code still has to pass a licensed broker before it can legally reach U.S. Customs and Border Protection. “Our volumes are up 40% annually. And headcount’s only up 5%, so you can see the AI’s working,” Petersen said. The interview followed Flexport’s fall technology release, which added an AI classification tool to its customs software and rail, barge and air routing to its free Flexport Atlas map. Time magazine named Flexport’s Customs Technology Suite to its Best Inventions of 2026 list on Oct. 15. AI classification still needs a licensed broker Classifying goods under the Harmonized Tariff Schedule is “the hardest problem in customs,” Petersen said. Flexport’s new tool suggests a 10-digit code and links the CBP rulings behind it. Federal law limits who can do that work for someone else. In a Jan. 16 ruling, CBP found that a foreign online platform was conducting customs business when its AI tool derived tariff subheadings beyond the six-digit level for goods that would be entered. articles.content: SAIA's Record $982.5M Q3 Revenue | What's Next? - FreightWaves SAIA President & CEO Fritz Holgrefe breaks down the company’s impressive third-quarter earnings, including record revenue and significant improvements in customer satisfaction and claims ratios. Discover how strategic network investments and a customer-centric approach are driving SAIA’s success and what lies ahead for the logistics giant. Saia reported record third-quarter revenue of $982.5 million, up 17% year over year, with earnings per share of $3.41, the LTL carrier’s president and CEO said in an interview with FreightWaves. Alongside the results, the company announced a $250 million share repurchase program — a signal that years of heavy network investment are giving way to a phase focused on profitability and capital returns. The revenue gain was driven by a combination of fuel surcharges, core pricing initiatives, and tonnage growth. Tonnage per workday rose approximately 8.9% year over year, reaching a record, while revenue per shipment climbed 5.8%. Shipments per workday, however, grew less than 1%, a deliberate outcome of the carrier’s effort to attract higher-weight freight from customers that value premium service. Service metrics underpinned the financial results. The company’s claims ratio fell 40% year over year, and its internally tracked Net Promoter Score improved 15% over the same period. articles.content: Beverage Distribution: Why Your SKU Count is Crushing Productivity - FreightWaves SKU proliferation has made beverage distribution a logistical nightmare. Zac Boehm, Chief Automation Officer at Hy-Tek Intralogistics, breaks down how their innovative automation systems, High-Sync and High-Flow, tackle the challenges of rising product counts and high labor turnover. Learn how optimizing pick paths and simplifying operations can lead to double or even triple pick speeds and a more efficient workforce. Hy-Tek Intralogistics has introduced two automation systems — Hy-Sync and Hy-Flow — designed specifically for beverage distributors struggling to manage exploding SKU counts and chronic labor turnover. The systems aim to shorten pick paths, protect on-time truck departures, and reduce the physical demands on warehouse workers, according to Zac Boehm, Chief Automation Officer at Hy-Tek Intralogistics. The core problem, Boehm said, is that distribution facilities built for hundreds of SKUs are now expected to handle thousands. articles.content: CN 3Q profit rises 6% as freight revenue climbs - FreightWaves Canadian National Railway reported a 6% increase in third-quarter profit Friday as stronger grain, energy and automotive freight activity lifted revenue, while higher fuel costs and a technology write-down weighed on reported margins. The Montreal-based railway (NYSE: CNI) maintained its full-year earnings outlook, saying growth was tracking toward the upper end of its forecast range. CN earned C$1.209 billion ($866 million), or $1.43 per diluted share, in the three months ended Sept. 30, compared with $816 million, or $1.31 a share, a year earlier. Revenue increased 15% to $3.42 billion from $2.98 billion. Adjusted diluted earnings rose 18% to approximately $1.55 a share, excluding a software impairment and rail-merger-related advisory expenses. That exceeded analysts’ expectations of about $1.50 a share, according to FactSet figures reported by Dow Jones. Revenue also topped the approximately $3.34 billion forecast. Freight revenue increased 15% to approximately $3.28 billion. Grain and fertilizer revenue rose 19% to $661 million, petroleum and chemicals revenue increased 17% to $716 million, and automotive revenue jumped 31% to $203 million. Revenue ton-miles increased 4%. Grain and fertilizer traffic rose 12% on that basis, while automotive traffic increased 20%. articles.content: Swedish owner Veritas books up to six chemical tankers in China - Splash247 Nantong Rainbow Offshore & Engineering Equipment Swedish shipowner Veritas Tankers has placed an order for up to six 13,000 dwt stainless steel chemical tankers at China’s Nantong Rainbow Offshore & Engineering Equipment, in a deal potentially worth $248m. The yard’s Shenzhen-listed parent, Jiangsu Rainbow Heavy Industries, confirmed the contract with an unnamed European owner in a stock exchange filing, putting the total value of the six-ship package, including options, at CNY1.5bn to CNY1.65bn ($225m to $248m). Shipbroking sources identify Sweden’s Rederi AB Veritas Tankers as the buyer, although the shipowner has not publicly confirmed its involvement. Rainbow has withheld the customer’s identity on commercial confidentiality grounds. The Chinese group has not specified how many vessels are firm and how many remain optional, but said deliveries are scheduled to begin 28 months after the contract is signed. The newbuildings are intended for parcel chemical trades, with designs suited to restricted waterways and operating conditions in northern Europe. For Rainbow, the deal adds another European customer to its chemical tanker business. The Nantong yard previously secured a contract from Germany’s John T. articles.content: Evalend drops newcastlemax option at Dajin Heavy - Splash247 Greek shipowner Evalend Shipping has been linked to the decision not to exercise an option for a fourth 211,000 dwt newcastlemax bulker at China’s Dajin Heavy Industry, removing a potential CNY525m ($78m) vessel from the yard’s order pipeline. Dajin disclosed that the option under a three-plus-one shipbuilding agreement signed in July had expired and that the Greek customer had elected not to proceed after discussions between the parties. The three firm ships, valued at a combined CNY1.575bn (about $235m), remain on order at subsidiary Tangshan Dajin, with completion scheduled across 2029 and 2030. The original deal carried a maximum value of CNY2.1bn ($313m) if the additional ship was declared. The yard said the decision does not constitute a contractual breach or trigger penalties. Dajin also expects no material impact on its production schedule or 2026 financial performance. The Chinese group did not identify the customer in its filing. However, Chinese shipbuilding market reports have linked the contract to Kriton Lendoudis-led Evalend Shipping. Splash covered the original agreement in July when Evalend emerged as the reported buyer of the three-plus-one series, marking the Greek owner’s entry into the newcastlemax sector. articles.content: China Merchants tanker arm targets Yangtze fleet renewal - Splash247 China Merchants-controlled Nanjing Tanker is planning to invest up to RMB191.72m ($28.7m) in ten 4,000 dwt crude oil barges as it moves to upgrade its fleet serving refineries along the Yangtze River. The Shanghai-listed owner has approved the investment through wholly owned subsidiary Nanjing Yangtze River Oil Transport Logistics, with Hunan Jinhang Shipbuilding selected to construct the vessels. The barges will be fitted with cargo oil pumps to support self-unloading operations, responding to demand from petrochemical and refinery customers along the waterway. Construction is scheduled to proceed in batches through 2027, according to the company’s filing. The project received unanimous board approval but still requires shareholder consent before proceeding. Nanjing Tanker operates across domestic coastal, river and international oil transportation markets. The China Merchants Group-controlled company has a fleet of more than 70 vessels, including crude and product tankers. The proposed barges form a separate investment from the company’s recently disclosed LR2 tanker expansion at Dalian Shipbuilding Industry Corporation. That four-vessel, methanol-ready LR2 programme was previously reported by Splash.
